items.description: Tessaoua is an important market town where agriculture forms the backbone of the local economy, particularly through cereal and onion cultivation.
Birni N'Konni provides essential social and educational services for the local youth population, acting as a key connector between rural and urban life.
Madaoua is situated in an agricultural zone known for traditional mixed farming practices and livestock integration.
The areas near Téra, near the border, host diverse bird habitats within the Sahelian landscape, serving as a transit point for avian migration.
Kollo benefits from the fertile Niger River valley, allowing for productive fruit farming, including varieties such as mangoes.
The town of Say, located on the Niger River, is historically linked to water-based activities and riverside agriculture.
Fishing along the river systems in the N'Gourti/Gouré zones represents a traditional livelihood for communities utilizing seasonal water bodies.
Birni provides a range of community support and children's programs, facilitating social cohesion in this regional administrative center.
Magaria is well-known for its contribution to local agricultural output, specializing in drought-resistant crops suitable for the regional climate.
Agriculture in the Mayahi area is fundamental, characterized by small-scale farming that supports local markets with diverse harvest products.
Gaya is a hub for agricultural trade, taking advantage of its favorable climate to support intensive farming along the river.
